name: GStreamer
summary: A multimedia framework that composes typed elements through pads into bins and pipelines, negotiates media capabilities across links, and drives processing through explicit element state transitions.

features.name: Element and pad media topology
features.description: The fixed source models GstElement as the processing unit and GstPad as its directional connection point. Official documentation describes pads as the ports through which elements expose data flow and are linked into a pipeline topology.
benefits: Makes media flow and connection direction explicit
Allows elements to expose compatible source and sink interfaces
costs: Pad availability and link direction constrain graph construction
Dynamic pads require application handling of topology changes

features.name: Caps negotiation boundary
features.description: GStreamer pads carry negotiated capabilities describing media types and formats. The official application-development documentation makes caps negotiation part of linking and data-flow setup, allowing adjacent elements to agree on a compatible representation.
benefits: Makes media compatibility a checked graph boundary
Supports pipelines that adapt formats between specialized elements
costs: Negotiation can reject an otherwise topologically valid link
Converters and fixated caps add setup and runtime complexity

features.name: Bin and pipeline composition
features.description: The fixed GstBin implementation contains child elements, intercepts child messages, and propagates state. GstPipeline extends the bin composition boundary with clock, bus, and top-level media execution behavior, as described by the official pipeline documentation.
benefits: Groups elements into reusable and manageable subgraphs
Provides a top-level lifecycle and message boundary for an application
costs: Nested ownership and message propagation add lifecycle rules
Pipeline behavior depends on child state and scheduling readiness

features.name: Element state transition model
features.description: The fixed GstElement source exposes current and pending states, state-change transitions, and asynchronous state-change results. Official documentation defines the NULL, READY, PAUSED, and PLAYING states and the transition contract used by pipelines and elements.
benefits: Makes resource activation and media execution phases explicit
Lets bins coordinate child state changes through a common lifecycle
costs: Async transitions require applications to observe pending and failure states
Element-specific state behavior can make pipeline startup ordering-sensitive

mathematical_views.question: Which element and pad graph topologies can carry compatible media from source to sink?
assumptions: Elements are nodes and linked pads are directed edges
Edges carry media constrained by caps
Plugin algorithms and buffer scheduling are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: How do bins and pipelines compose child elements while propagating messages, clocks, and lifecycle state?
assumptions: A bin is a container node with child element nodes
A pipeline is a top-level bin with application-facing execution services
Message and clock internals are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which element and pipeline states are reachable through coordinated state changes and asynchronous completion?
assumptions: States form a transition system with pending transitions
Child state changes constrain parent progress
The model does not claim every plugin has identical transition behavior

benefits: Explicit pads make media flow composable
costs: Dynamic topology and link direction increase graph-management work

benefits: Format compatibility is negotiated at connections
costs: Negotiation failures and conversion elements complicate setup

benefits: Subgraphs gain reusable ownership and lifecycle boundaries
costs: Nested message, clock, and state propagation add coordination

benefits: Common states coordinate activation and playback
costs: Asynchronous and plugin-specific transitions complicate startup
